pool_config.pool_brief: Build an array-based data processing system for a Nigerian business context. Your solution must use: array access with index (including last-element pattern), push or pop or shift or unshift, splice or slice, map to transform an array, filter to subset an array, and forEach or for...of to iterate and display results. All variables must use const or let (no var).

projects.title: Konga Product Catalogue Manager
projects.scenario: Build a product catalogue management system for a Konga seller. Process the provided inventory using array methods.
requirements: Print the first product name, last product price, and total catalogue count using array access
Add two new products to the end with push, then remove the last one with pop (print what was popped)
Use splice to replace the out-of-stock product at index 2 with a new available product
Use map to create a new array of product name strings formatted as: 'Wireless Earbuds — ₦4500'
Use filter to get only in-stock products, then forEach to print a numbered list of available products

projects.title: Publica Academy Student Cohort Tracker
projects.scenario: Build a student cohort management system for Publica Academy. Process the provided student dataset using array methods.
requirements: Print the first student's name, last student's score, and total cohort size using array access
Add two new students to the cohort with push, then remove the last one with pop (print the removed student's name)
Use splice to remove the student at index 1 (a duplicate entry) from the list
Use map to create an array of result strings formatted as: 'Amara Obi — 88 — Pass' (Pass if score >= 50, Fail otherwise)
Use filter to get only passing students (score >= 50), then forEach to print a numbered list

projects.title: PiggyVest Transaction Manager
projects.scenario: Build a transaction management system for a PiggyVest savings account. Process the provided transaction dataset using array methods.
requirements: Print the first transaction ID, last transaction amount, and total transaction count using array access
Add a new deposit to the end with push, then remove the last transaction (the most recent) with pop and print it
Use slice to extract the last 3 transactions (most recent) and print them as a 'Recent Activity' report
Use map to create an array of transaction summary strings: 'TXN-001: +₦5000 (savings)' for deposits and 'TXN-002: -₦1500 (spending)' for withdrawals
Use filter to get only deposits, then forEach to sum and print the total deposited amount

projects.title: Paystack Payment Batch Dashboard
projects.scenario: Build a payment batch dashboard for a Paystack merchant. Process the provided payment dataset using array methods.
requirements: Print the first payment merchant name, last payment amount, and total payment count using array access
Simulate a refund by removing the last payment with pop (print refunded amount); then add a new replacement payment with push
Use slice to get a preview of the first 3 payments for a dashboard summary
Use map to create an array of payment labels: 'Shoprite: ₦15000 ✔' for success and 'GTBank: ₦50000 ✖' for failed
Use filter to get successful payments only, then forEach to calculate and print total successful revenue

projects.title: Bolt Driver Trip History Analyser
projects.scenario: Build a trip history analyser for a Bolt driver. Process the provided trips dataset using array methods.
requirements: Print the first trip ID, last trip fare, and total trip count using array access
Add a new high-earning trip to the end with push; then pop it back off (print the popped trip's fare — simulating a cancelled booking)
Use splice to remove the lowest-rated trip (at index 4, rating 2.5) from the history
Use map to create an array of trip summary strings: 'TRIP-001: ₦1800 — 4.8★'
Use filter to get high-rated trips (rating >= 4.5), then forEach to calculate and print total earnings from high-rated trips

descriptors.full: Array access uses correct index patterns (including last-element), push/pop/shift/unshift used correctly and print the expected outputs, splice or slice applied correctly
descriptors.partial: Most operations correct but one method produces wrong output or is missing
descriptors.none: Multiple access or mutation operations missing or producing incorrect results

descriptors.full: map correctly transforms every element into the required format and returns a new array, filter correctly keeps only matching elements, neither mutates the original
descriptors.partial: One of the two works correctly, the other has errors or attempts mutation
descriptors.none: map and/or filter missing or producing incorrect results

descriptors.full: forEach or for...of correctly iterates the filtered/processed result and output matches the required format
descriptors.partial: Iteration works but output format has minor errors
descriptors.none: Iteration missing or does not produce output

descriptors.full: const/let used correctly, descriptive variable names, output matches requirements exactly
descriptors.none: var used, unclear names, or significantly malformed output
